sources.title: Equinix Q3 2026 earnings presentation (28 October 2026), slide 35 Data Center Portfolio Composition - AMER, slide 30 Adjusted NOI Composition and slide 47 Definitions
sources.summary: Equinix's Q3 2026 earnings presentation (49 slides), linked from its results release of 28 October 2026 for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. Slide 36, 'Data Center Portfolio Composition - EMEA', has the row 'Johannesburg | 1 |' with JN1 in the Expansion column (not Stabilized, New or Acquisition) and JN1 in the Owned column without the asterisk that marks a long-term ground lease; the same slide lists Lagos (LG1 Stabilized, LG2 Expansion; LG1*, LG2* owned subject to ground lease), Accra (AC1 Stabilized, AC1*) and Abidjan (AB1 Stabilized, AB1*). Its Status Change rows are empty, the EMEA change summary names only PA12x, and the footnotes say the stabilized/expansion/new categorisation is reset annually in Q1. Slide 47 defines Expansion Data Centers as those whose Phase 1 began operating before 1 January 2025 with an expected expansion of one or more additional phases (or a redevelopment), and New Data Centers as those whose Phase 1 began operating on or after 1 January 2025. The presentation thus states that JN1 is an Equinix IBX data center in its operating portfolio at the quarter end, with its first phase operating since before 2025 and further phases expected. No address, capacity per IBX or opening date is given.

sources.title: Iron Mountain Q3 2026 Supplemental Financial Information (Data Center Operating Portfolio and Expansion and Development Activity)
sources.summary: Iron Mountain's Q3 2026 Supplemental Financial Information (29 pages; PDF created 5 November 2026), released with its third-quarter results on 5 November 2026 for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. Page 22, 'Data Center Operating Portfolio', lists by market the facilities in Iron Mountain's operating portfolio with Stabilized, Pre-Stabilized and Total leaseable MW and leased %. Its European rows are: Amsterdam 'AMS-1' 13.1 MW (Stabilized, 99.2% leased); London 'LON-1' 8.7 MW (Stabilized, 51.4% leased) and 'LON-2' 27.0 MW (Stabilized, 100.0% leased); Frankfurt 'FRA-1 (2)' 27.0 MW and 'FRA-2' 9.8 MW (both Stabilized, 100.0% leased; footnote 2: FRA-1 is held by an unconsolidated joint venture); Madrid 'MAD-1' 3.0 MW (Stabilized, 50.3% leased). None of these rows has Pre-Stabilized capacity. The same page gives a Total Potential Capacity of 544.6 MW in the Operating Portfolio, 317.1 MW Under Construction and 511.9 MW Held for Development. Page 23, 'Data Center Expansion and Development Activity', lists 'AMS-1 Phase 4' (10.0 MW under construction, expected completion Q2 2027), 'AMS-2' (20.0 MW held for development), 'LON-3 Future Phases' (24.7 MW, expected completion Q1 2027), 'MAD-2/3' (20.0 MW, expected completion Q1 2028) and 'MAD Future Phases' (56.0 MW held for development); it has no LON-1 or MAD-1 row. The Data Center Business Definitions (page 28) define Leaseable MW as critical power capacity available for customer use and Pre-Stabilized as 'A building recently placed in service which has not yet reached 85% leased or 24 months in service', so every row of the operating-portfolio table is a facility in service. The table is thus Iron Mountain's dated statement that AMS-1, LON-1 and MAD-1 were operating data centres in its portfolio at 30 September 2026. No address, opening date or building outline is given, and the leaseable MW are not measured load.
